title: Delta Detective lab memo
body:
Summary:

This is a working memo from the Delta Detective lab — a compact, pragmatic playbook to triage token-latency regressions surfaced via our perf sentinel pipelines and canary diffs. The goal is to capture quick experiments, signals, and an explicit bisect + rollback decision tree so on-call and on-call-adjacent engineers can act without waiting for a long postmortem.

Situation snapshot (example case):
- Alert: model-x@canary-us-west p95 token latency increased from 120ms -> 300ms (observed 2026-02-17 03:14 UTC).
- Signal source: route-level Alert (perf-sentinel) — drift flagged by canary vs baseline sampling.
- Immediate impact: 0.8% error budget burn for SLA group, some user requests timed out.
- Canary is 4% of traffic, baseline (prod) unchanged at first glance.

What to collect first (fast evidence kit):
1) Canary vs baseline time-series snapshot (last 24h): p50/p95/p99 token latency, request rate, 5xx rate, CPU/GPU utilization, NVInactive memory, and queue depth.
2) Representative traces (all levels) for slow requests — sample 50 traces from both cohorts.
3) Mini-bench: run the golden-corpus (20 prompts with varying seq len) against the canary binary and baseline binary with 5 repeats each. Capture latencies and stdout logs.
4) Sample host-level metrics: iostat, dmesg, out-of-memory messages, GPU SM utilization, clock throttling events.
5) Recent deployments/config changes: last 48h in canary and infra config updates.

Quick PromQL queries to paste into the investigation dashboard:
- p95 token latency for route: 
  sum by(route) (histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(token_latency_bucket[15m])) by (le, route)))
- request rate and 5xx: 
  sum(rate(http_requests_total{status=~"5..",route=~"model-x.*"}[5m])) by (route)
  sum(rate(http_requests_total{route=~"model-x.*"}[5m])) by (route)
- KV cache hit rate (per model): 
  sum(rate(kv_cache_hits_total[5m])) / sum(rate(kv_cache_requests_total[5m]))

High-level suspect matrix (quick mental model):
- New kernel / runtime commit in canary (code path change).
- Model binary variant/quantization switch in canary.
- Autoscaler or batching policy change causing microbursts and queueing.
- Hardware/driver regression (GPU driver update, power management).
- Workload shift (longer sequences, more streaming responses).
- Downstream dependency slowdown (redis/kv store for prefix cache).

Investigation flow (short, prescriptive):
1) Validate alert with independent sampling: run a controlled curl load against canary route from a different region (to rule out router-level noise). Compare median of the mini-bench.
2) Pair traces: align 10 slow traces from canary with 10 fast baseline traces and open a diff view (fields: token time series, kernel timeline, batching windows, kv cache hits).
3) Reproduce on a reserved node: spin up the exact canary binary and baseline binary on identical hardware, replay the same request log (capture of 200 requests) with our replay harness.
4) Profile hot paths: run async CPU profilers and GPU tracing on the replay harness. Collect per-token breakdown: tokenization, embedding lookup, attention kernel 1, attention kernel 2, softmax, sampling.

Profiling commands / artifacts we like: (copy-paste friendly)
- start replay harness (local): 
  ./replay --model model-x --input-corpus golden-corpus.json --concurrency 1 --repeat 5 --emit-traces traces/
- CPU flame: run py-spy or linux perf on the serving binary during replay.
  sudo perf record -F 99 -g -p $(pidof serving-runtime) -- sleep 30
  sudo perf script > perf.out
- GPU kernel timeline: use nvprof / Nsight CLI on the worker container (note: might require maintenance window).
- KV cache tracing: enable kv_cache.debug=1 and capture request/response latencies to redis (if used).

Bisect plan (code/config):
- If a single deploy is the likely window: binary search through canary deploys (start from oldest->newest) using the replay harness. We accept a 15–30 minute run per candidate.
- If throughput/batching policy changed: toggle batching thresholds (0.5x, 1x, 2x) on canary and rerun the golden-corpus. Watch for non-linear improvements (indicative of batching-induced queueing).
- If model quantization is suspect: test default FP16 vs quantized variant on the same hardware; measure per-token variance.

Statistical checks to avoid chasing noise:
- Use paired t-test on per-prompt latencies between baseline and canary runs (n >= 30 prompts recommended).
- Look for consistent median shift across multiple independent runs before escalating.

Decision rubric (actionable outputs):
- Immediate rollback: if p95 delta > 2x AND reproduces locally on identical hardware within 30m, rollback canary deploy and open an incident.
- Mitigation: if root cause is batching/config, adjust batching thresholds for canary and observe for 30m.
- Monitor-only: if signal is weak (p95 drift < 1.3x and not reproducible), set short-term higher sampling (5x traces) and revisit.

Example triage notes (how I would fill a quick case):
- symptoms: p95 spike to 300ms, p50 stable ~110ms, error rate unchanged.
- initial hypothesis: microqueueing introduced by batching threshold bump in canary.
- quick test: run replay harness with batching=1x vs batching=2x -> observed 1.9x p95 at 2x; confirms microqueueing.
- action: set canary batching back to 1x, monitor 15m, note rollback if not improving.

Artifacts to attach to the incident ticket:
- golden-corpus bench results CSV (canary vs baseline)
- 20 paired traces and a short summary table with suspect stage durations
- perf flame, nvprof summary, and any kernel version info
- diff of last 5 canary deploy manifests and infra changes

Open questions & TODOs (lab):
- Add a standard Golden Corpus for short vs long sequence distributions (owner: Priya).
- Automate the replay harness to accept a canary tag and run a pre-bisect sanity check. (owner: Marcus)
- Add a dashboard panel that overlays canary p95 vs baseline p95 with a non-parametric significance test (owner: Diego).

Closing notes (for the on-call):
- The Delta Detective lab memo is intentionally compact — prefer experiments that complete in <30m and leave evidence in the incident ticket. If you hit a cross-cutting infra suspect (driver/kernel), escalate to infra SRE early.
- If rollback is chosen, capture a canary snapshot bundle (logs, traces, perf) and tag it to the PR so the originating author has artifacts to investigate.

Appendix: Useful links and commands
- replay harness repo: github.com/redwood-inference/replay-harness (runbook in README)
- perf guide: docs/internal/perf-playbook (Confluence-8251)
- quick query generator: docs/internal/query-templates

Notes to self (rough):
- Remember to add standard CSV schema for bench results (col: prompt_id, seq_len, lat_ms, cohort).
- Consider adding a small “canary smoke” test that runs golden-corpus after every canary deploy and posts results to the canary channel.
